sources.entry: pgvector - pgvector support for Python, adding vector types and similarity search to psycopg, asyncpg, SQLAlchemy, and Django.

summary.one_liner: A Python package that adds pgvector support (vector, half-vector, bit, and sparse vector types plus similarity search) to PostgreSQL drivers and ORMs such as Django, SQLAlchemy, Psycopg, asyncpg, pg8000, and Peewee.
summary.what_it_does: The package registers pgvector column types and distance operators with several Python PostgreSQL libraries, so vectors can be stored and queried from Python code. Supported integrations are Django, SQLAlchemy, SQLModel, Psycopg 3, Psycopg 2, asyncpg, pg8000, and Peewee. Each integration provides nearest-neighbor ordering by L2, inner product, cosine, L1, Hamming, or Jaccard distance, plus distance annotation and threshold filtering. It also covers aggregate averaging and summing of vectors and creating HNSW or IVFFlat approximate indexes, including half-precision indexing in Django. A standalone Vector, HalfVector, and SparseVector API converts to and from lists, NumPy arrays, and SciPy sparse arrays. The README also links to many example projects, such as RAG with Ollama, embeddings with OpenAI, and recommendations with LightFM.
use_cases: store embeddings in PostgreSQL from Python
nearest-neighbor search in a Django model
semantic search over documents stored in Postgres
approximate nearest neighbor indexing with HNSW or IVFFlat
how_to_run: Enable the pgvector extension in your database (CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector)
Follow the README section for your database library (Django, SQLAlchemy, Psycopg, asyncpg, pg8000, or Peewee)
Register the vector types on your connection, then insert and query vectors
notable: Covers eight Python database libraries with one package
Supports vector, half-vector, bit, and sparse vector types
Django half-precision HNSW indexing via OpClass and Cast
Includes many example projects for embeddings, hybrid search, and recommendations
Converts to and from NumPy and SciPy sparse arrays
caveats: Requires a PostgreSQL database with the pgvector extension installed
Development and example runs need a local PostgreSQL instance (createdb) and the dev dependency group
